name: Jabs don't pass the turn
citation: library/mk2/arcade.frames.json: mileena/HP/far/gap_px 71 -> on_hit +4, on_block +13, damage 11, hitstop 0 (high confidence). reptile/HK/far -> damage 32 (the counter Reptile attempts).
claim: Mileena's far HP is +13 ON BLOCK. A blocked jab does not give the turn back: she acts again 13 frames before Reptile can, so a jab loop is a true blockstring, and the frame Reptile spends trying to take his turn is the frame he gets hit.

beats.name: jab-1-blocked
beats.note: far HP at gap 71; contact f11; chip 3 (blocked contact chips, docs/frames.md 2.6 -- zero damage would mean WHIFF).

beats.name: jab-2-blocked
beats.note: pressed at global f19 -- Mileena's OWN earliest actionable frame after the blocked jab (measured: f19 works, f15-f18 do not). Reptile drops guard at contact+1 to arm his counter (punish.py's guard-release law).

beats.name: jab-3-stuffs-the-counter
beats.note: Reptile's earliest actionable frame after jab 2 is global f51 (= contact f30 + 21). Mileena steps in and jabs at her own f44; contact f55 beats his f59 -- he takes a full 11 (a HIT, not the 3 chip) and lands nothing. The CONTROL (same defender program, no jab 3) is in VERIFICATION.md: his HK lands 32 on her.

notes: Rung: m-gap-39 (.gap.json gap_px 71, char ids 5 vs 9, inputs_live both). Gap is part of the move's identity: at gap <= 63 the same button is Mileena's CLOSE HP (24 damage, -2 on block).
Pushback is real: each blocked far HP adds +9 px, so jab 3 needs a 5-frame step-in to stay inside far HP's 83 px connect range.

A CHAIN window also exists and is deliberately not used here: a second far HP pressed at f12/f13/f14 comes out immediately (contact f23/f24/f25), while f15-f18 produce nothing and f19 is her own earliest free re-press. The sequence uses f19 because that is the frame the +13 number is about.
